title: Harbison Protection Contracts Sales Rule Sheet: Who Can Buy, When and on What Equipment
content:
**1. The included workmanship warranty.** The Harbison 2-Year Workmanship Warranty, the tier issued at no charge with every installation, is issued with the purchase channel "with installation" on the day every Harbison installation is completed. It covers the new equipment as a matched system when an indoor and an outdoor unit were installed together. It can never be bought separately.

**2. A tier bought on the installation contract.** A higher tier bought on the installation contract is billed on the installation project as a labor warranty upgrade and issued, with the purchase channel "with installation", on the day the installation is completed.

**3. Post-installation purchase.** A post-installation purchase is accepted only when the date of handling is no later than the tier's post-installation purchase window, in calendar days, after the installation was completed. Purchase-window days are counted as calendar days with the installed date as day 0, and a purchase on the last day of the window is accepted. A post-installation purchase needs no inspection and is open only on equipment Harbison installed, on tiers whose window is above 0.

**4. Aftermarket purchase on existing equipment.** An aftermarket purchase is open only on tiers that allow aftermarket purchase, only for a brand on the tier's eligible-brand list, and only after an inspection billed at the tier's aftermarket inspection fee. An aftermarket purchase is accepted only when the date of handling is no later than the tier's oldest equipment age, in years, after the equipment was installed. Aftermarket age is counted in calendar months, as the age in years times twelve added to the equipment install date, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist; a purchase dated on that boundary is accepted.

**5. Matched systems.** For a matched-system scope every age and window rule applies to both units, and the matched-system scope is open only where the tier makes it available.

**6. Equipment in service.** The covered equipment must be in service at the holder's address.

**7. Transfers.** Contracts issued by transfer follow the home-sale transfer terms only.

**Evidence and clocks.**

| Rule | Clock starts | Record that proves it | Boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Post-installation window | the installation was completed | the installed date on the Harbison installation project | last day of the window accepted |
| Aftermarket age | the equipment was installed | the install date on the equipment register | the boundary date accepted |
| Equipment in service | — | the unit's status on the equipment register shows it in service | — |

All three are read from the company's records before the purchase is accepted.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, using a 365-day window and a 7-year age).**

- Installation completed 10 March 2025 (day 0). Day 365 is 10 March 2026: a purchase handled that day is accepted; one handled on 11 March 2026 is not.
- Equipment installed 28 February 2019. Seven years is 84 calendar months, giving 28 February 2026: a purchase dated 28 February 2026 is accepted; one dated 1 March 2026 is not.
- Equipment installed 29 February 2016. Adding 84 months reaches 29 February 2023, a date that does not exist, so the boundary falls back to 28 February 2023: a purchase dated 28 February 2023 is accepted; one dated 1 March 2023 is not.
- A matched system whose indoor unit was installed within the age limit but whose outdoor unit was installed before it fails the age rule, because the rule applies to both units.
